newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Nicaragua seeks Taiwan help to build port.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua seeks Taiwan help to build port.

text.p: Nicaragua, one of the 30 states that recognise Taipei instead of its arch-rival Beijing, on Wednesday asked Taiwan to help develop a port project.

"One of the projects we are presenting to the Republic of China (on Taiwan) is to receive some help to develop the Port of Corinto," visiting Nicaraguan Foreign Minister Emilio Alvarez Montalvan told reporters.
Montalvan is accompanying President Arnoldo Aleman on a five-day state visit to Taiwan.
Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang was non-committal, saying Taipei was still evaluating the issue.
Aleman's visit came after Nicaragua's U.N. ambassador, Enrique Paguaga Fernandez, last week denounced threats by China against his country's support for Taiwan's membership.
Beijing took over China's U.N. seat in 1971 when Taiwan, to which the Nationalist Chinese government retreated in 1949 following a civil war, was expelled from the United Nations.
China regards the island as a renegade province and reacts fiercely to any move to recognise or seat Taiwan.
In July Nicaragua and eight other allies of Taiwan signed a letter asking the General Assembly to discuss granting Taiwan U.N. membership during its opening session in September.
China prevented similar proposals from winning inscription on the U.N. agenda for four consecutive years.
Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui will embark on a two-week tour to central American nations in September.

Lee in 1995 made a private but high-profile visit to the United States that prompted Beijing to launch months of intimidating war games and unarmed missile tests near Taiwan to warn the island against opting for independence.
